steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Simple time divides beats into 2 (2/4, 3/4, 4/4); compound time divides into 3 (6/8, 9/8, 12/8) — the feel is fundamentally different.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Syncopation places emphasis on off-beats or weak beats — it creates rhythmic tension and is central to jazz, blues and popular music.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Polyrhythm is two or more conflicting rhythmic patterns played simultaneously — common in African and Caribbean music traditions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hemiola creates a temporary shift of metre (e.g. feeling 2 groups of 3 as 3 groups of 2) — used from Renaissance to pop music.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how rhythm metre and tempo are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use rhythm metre and tempo. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use rhythm metre and tempo in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how rhythm metre and tempo are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language | A practical application showing understanding of how rhythm metre and tempo can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
